title: Enforcement Decree of the Korea Veterans Welfare and Healthcare Corporation Act
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE KOREA VETERANS WELFARE AND HEALTHCARE CORPORATION ACT

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Korea Veterans Welfare and Healthcare Corporation Act and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Registration of Establishment)
(1) The Korea Veterans Welfare and Healthcare Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the "Corporation") under Article 2 of the Korea Veterans Welfare and Healthcare Corporation Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") shall register its establishment within three weeks from the date on which its articles of incorporation are authorized.
(2) The matters to be registered for establishment under paragraph (1) shall be as follows:
1. Purpose;
2. Name;
3. Location of the principal office;
4. Names and addresses of executive officers;
5. Matters concerning the authority of representation;
6. Method of public announcement.

Article 3 (Registration of Relocation)
Where the Corporation relocates its principal office, it shall register the new location and the date of relocation at either the former or the new location within two weeks after relocation.

Article 4 (Registration of Changes)
Where any of the matters registered under the subparagraphs of Article 2 (2) changes (excluding cases constituting registration of relocation under Article 3), the Corporation shall register the changes within three weeks after the change.

Article 5 (Documents to Be Attached to Applications for Registration)
An application for registration under Articles 2 through 4 shall be accompanied by the applicable documents specified in the following categories:
1. Registration of establishment under Article 2 (1): The Corporation's articles of incorporation;
2. Registration of changes under Article 3: Documents proving the changes;
3. Registration of relocation under Article 4: Documents proving the relocation.

Article 6 (Calculation of Registration Periods)
For matters to be registered under Articles 2 through 4 that require authorization from the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, the registration period shall be calculated from the date on which the written authorization is received. <Amended on April 11, 2023>

Article 7 (Effect of Registrations Other than Registration of Establishment)
Matters requiring registration other than registration of establishment may not be asserted against a third party unless registered.

Article 8 (Duties of the Auditor)
(1) The duties of the auditor shall be as follows:
1. Auditing the condition of the Corporation's property;
2. Auditing accounting and affairs related thereto;
3. Auditing other matters prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
(2) Where an audit reveals any irregularity or deficiency, the auditor shall report that fact to the board of directors and the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs without delay. <Amended on April 11, 2023>
(3) Matters concerning the methods and procedures for performing the auditor's duties and related matters shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 9 (Ex Officio Non-Executive Directors)
The non-executive directors who are public officials of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs and the Ministry of Planning and Budget under Article 8 (3) 1 and 2 of the Act shall be the head of the Planning and Coordination Office and the director-general in charge of the Corporation's affairs at the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, and the deputy director-general in charge of budget affairs in the social sector at the Ministry of Planning and Budget. <Amended on September 22, 2020; April 11, 2023; December 30, 2025>

Article 10 (Meetings of the Board of Directors)
(1) Meetings of the board of directors shall be divided into regular meetings and special meetings.
(2) Regular meetings shall be convened as prescribed by the articles of incorporation, and special meetings shall be convened where the chairperson of the Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the "chairperson") deems it necessary or at least one-third of the directors in office request a meeting.

Article 10-2 (Procedures for Recommending Candidates for Executive Directors)
(1) The Corporation shall have an Executive Director Recommendation Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Executive Director Recommendation Committee") to recommend candidates for executive directors pursuant to Article 8 (2) of the Act.
(2) The Executive Director Recommendation Committee shall consist of the following persons:
1. Two persons selected by the board of directors from among non-executive directors under Article 8 (3) 1 and 2 of the Act;
2. One person selected by the board of directors from among non-executive directors under Article 8 (3) 3 and 4 of the Act;
3. Two outside members selected by the board of directors who have extensive knowledge and experience concerning the Corporation's business.
(3) The chairperson of the Executive Director Recommendation Committee shall be elected by and from among its members.
(4) A meeting of the Executive Director Recommendation Committee shall be called to order with the attendance of at least two-thirds of its members, and resolutions shall be passed by the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present.
(5) The Executive Director Recommendation Committee shall recommend, without ranking, candidates for executive director numbering twice the number of positions to be filled. In such cases, it shall not recommend a member of the Executive Director Recommendation Committee as an executive director.
(6) Matters necessary for the operation of the Executive Director Recommendation Committee, including the examination of candidates, methods of recommendation, and disqualification, challenge, and recusal of members, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (5), shall be prescribed by the Corporation's articles of incorporation or internal regulations.

Article 11 (Remuneration and Other Matters concerning Educational Public Officials Holding Concurrent Positions)
(1) The chairperson may appoint educational public officials concurrently serving as medical personnel of the Corporation pursuant to Article 14 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "teachers holding concurrent positions") to positions at department-head level or above responsible for medical care at veterans hospitals under Article 7 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "veterans hospitals").
(2) Notwithstanding Article 6 of the Enforcement Decree of the Higher Education Act, teachers holding concurrent positions may be exempted from teaching hours or have their teaching hours reduced.
(3) The remuneration of teachers holding concurrent positions shall be paid by the universities to which they belong.
(4) The Corporation may pay allowances to teachers holding concurrent positions as prescribed by its articles of incorporation.
(5) Teachers holding concurrent positions shall comply with the Corporation's articles of incorporation and all its regulations and faithfully perform their duties.

Article 12 (Concurrent Positions of Private School Teachers)
(1) Where the chairperson deems it particularly necessary for medical care, the chairperson may have faculty members working at private medical colleges and dental colleges (hereinafter referred to as "private school teachers") concurrently serve as medical personnel of the Corporation, with their consent and the permission of the president or dean of their university or college.
(2) Article 11 (1) and (3) through (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis to private school teachers concurrently serving as medical personnel of the Corporation pursuant to paragraph (1).

Article 13 (Termination of Concurrent Positions)
The chairperson may order the termination of a concurrent position where a teacher holding a concurrent position or a private school teacher concurrently serving as medical personnel of the Corporation falls under any of the following:
1. Where the teacher violates Article 11 (5);
2. Where a teacher holding a concurrent position falls under any of the subparagraphs of Article 78 (1) of the State Public Officials Act;
3. Where a private school teacher falls under any of the subparagraphs of Article 61 (1) of the Private School Act.

Article 14 (Requests for Compensation Payments)
(1) Where the Corporation intends to request a budget for compensation payments under Article 16 of the Act, it shall submit to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, no later than eight months before the beginning of the business year, a request for compensation payments that classifies personnel expenses, material expenses, other expenses, and similar costs incurred in providing medical care, convalescence, and rehabilitative training to persons to whom the Acts referred to in Article 1 of the Act apply into medical care expenses, convalescence expenses, and rehabilitative training expenses, accompanied by the following documents (limited to the portions necessary for the request for compensation payments): <Amended on January 5, 2021; April 11, 2023>
1. A business plan;
2. A projected income statement and projected statement of financial position;
3. Other materials explaining the details of the request for compensation payments.
(2) Upon receipt of a request for compensation payments under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall reflect its contents in the budget. <Amended on April 11, 2023>
(3) When the budget for compensation payments has been finalized, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall notify the Corporation of its contents. <Amended on April 11, 2023>

Article 15 (Applications for Payment of Compensation)
Where the Corporation intends to receive compensation payments, it shall submit an application for payment of compensation to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, accompanied by a monthly budget execution plan. <Amended on April 11, 2023>

Article 15-2 (Claims for and Payment of Pharmaceutical Expenses)
(1) Where a pharmacist who has dispensed medicines to persons eligible for medical treatment and their surviving family members and family members pursuant to any of the following provisions claims pharmaceutical expenses [excluding cases where the duties of reviewing, adjusting, and assessing pharmaceutical expenses have been entrusted pursuant to Article 17-2(1)1 to the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service under Article 62 of the National Health Insurance Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Review and Assessment Service")], the Corporation shall verify the details of the claim and pay the pharmaceutical expenses within one month from the date of the claim: <Amended on June 27, 2012; August 31, 2012; September 13, 2016; April 6, 2021>
1. Article 64-2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State and Others (including cases where that Article applies mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 11(2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of Persons of Distinguished Service to Independence, Article 9(3) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of War Veterans and Establishment of Related Associations, Article 8(4) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Assistance to Patients Suffering from Actual or Potential Aftereffects of Defoliants and Establishment of Related Associations, and Article 23(2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Support for Discharged Soldiers Act);
2. Article 64 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Support for Persons Eligible for Veterans Compensation;
3. Article 35 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of Persons of Distinguished Service to the May 18 Democratization Movement and Establishment of Related Associations;
4. Article 37 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of Persons of Distinguished Service on Special Missions and Establishment of Related Associations.
(2) A pharmacist intending to claim pharmaceutical expenses under paragraph (1) shall submit to the Corporation a claim form for pharmaceutical expenses, accompanied by a detailed statement of pharmaceutical expenses containing the following matters:
1. The name and resident registration number of the person who received pharmaceutical benefits;
2. The name of the medical institution that issued the prescription and the prescription issuance number;
3. The names and quantities of the medicines dispensed;
4. The year, month, and day of dispensing;
5. The total pharmaceutical expenses, the amount borne by the Corporation, the amount borne by the National Health Insurance Service, and the amount borne by the patient.
(3) The forms of the claim form for pharmaceutical expenses and detailed statement of pharmaceutical expenses under paragraph (2), and instructions for their preparation, shall be determined by the Corporation.

Article 16 (Requests for Provision of Data)
(1) The term "data prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 24-2(1) of the Act means the data specified in the attached Table.
(2) When requesting the provision of data pursuant to Article 24-2(1) of the Act, the Corporation shall send the person from whom the data are requested a written request stating the legal basis for and reasons for the request, details of the data requested, and other relevant matters.
(3) Where the data specified in the attached Table are stored using a computerized recording device, such as a diskette, magnetic tape, microfilm, or optical disc, or a computer program, a person requested to provide data pursuant to Article 24-2(1) of the Act may provide the data in the form in which they are stored.
(4) The Corporation may establish and operate a related information system to efficiently process the data under paragraph (1) held by medical facilities designated by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs and entrusted with medical treatment. <Amended on April 11, 2023>

Article 17 Deleted. <October 15, 2009>

Article 17-2 (Entrustment of Duties)
(1) Pursuant to Article 24-3 of the Act, the Corporation shall entrust to the Review and Assessment Service the duties of reviewing, adjusting, and assessing the expenses borne by the State among the following expenses: <Amended on August 31, 2012; August 2, 2016; September 13, 2016; September 22, 2020; January 16, 2024>
1. Among the pharmaceutical expenses under Article 15-2, pharmaceutical expenses claimed by a pharmacist who has dispensed medicines to persons eligible for medical treatment in accordance with a prescription issued by a veterans hospital or a medical facility entrusted by the State with medical treatment (hereinafter referred to as an "entrusted hospital");
2. Medical expenses of entrusted hospitals for persons eligible for medical treatment;
3. Among the medical expenses of veterans hospitals for persons eligible for medical treatment, medical expenses that fall within the scope of medical care benefits under Article 41(3) of the National Health Insurance Act.
(2) The term "persons eligible for medical treatment" in paragraph (1) 1 through 3 means persons who have received medical treatment pursuant to any of the following provisions: <Amended on January 26, 2012; April 17, 2012; December 21, 2012; September 13, 2016; April 6, 2021; January 16, 2024>
1. Article 17 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of Persons of Distinguished Service to Independence;
2. Articles 42, 73, and 73-2 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State and Others, and Article 73-2 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State and Others (referring to that Act before its amendment by Act No. 11041);
3. Article 51 of the Act on Support for Persons Eligible for Veterans Compensation;
4. Article 34 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of Persons of Distinguished Service to the May 18 Democratization Movement and Establishment of Related Associations;
5. Article 7 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of War Veterans and Establishment of Related Associations;
6. Article 7(1) or (2) of the Act on Assistance to Patients Suffering from Actual or Potential Aftereffects of Defoliants and Establishment of Related Associations;
7. Article 33 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of Persons of Distinguished Service on Special Missions and Establishment of Related Associations;
8. Article 20 of the Support for Discharged Soldiers Act;
9. Other medical treatment deemed necessary by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs for the provision of medical treatment in island and remote areas.
(3) The Corporation may pay the Review and Assessment Service fees for the entrustment of duties under paragraph (1).
(4) Matters necessary for the methods and procedures for claiming expenses related to paragraph (1) shall be determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on April 11, 2023>

Article 18 (Processing of Sensitive Information and Unique Identifying Information)
Where unavoidable for performing any of the following affairs, the Corporation (including an institution entrusted with the Corporation's duties pursuant to Article 17-2) may process health information under Article 23 of the Personal Information Protection Act and data containing resident registration numbers, passport numbers, or alien registration numbers under Article 19, subparagraph 1, 2, or 4 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act: <Amended on April 11, 2023>
1. Affairs concerning claims for, review of, and payment of medical expenses borne by the State for persons of distinguished service to the State and others treated by the Corporation pursuant to Article 6, subparagraph 1 of the Act;
2. Affairs concerning the management of medical facilities entrusted with medical treatment by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs pursuant to Article 6, subparagraph 11 of the Act;
3. Affairs concerning the verification of documents provided pursuant to Article 24-2(2) of the Act relating to medical examinations of patients suffering from actual aftereffects of defoliants, patients suffering from potential aftereffects of defoliants, or second-generation patients suffering from aftereffects of defoliants.

Addenda <No. 10318, May 20, 1981>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Repeal of Legislation)
The Enforcement Decree of the Vocational Rehabilitation Act for Persons Eligible for Veterans Assistance shall be repealed on the date on which the Vocational Rehabilitation Act for Persons Eligible for Veterans Assistance is repealed pursuant to Article 2 of the Addenda to the Act; provided that Articles 19 through 36 shall remain effective until the date that is six months after the date of registration of the establishment of the Corporation.

Article 3 (Establishment Expenses)
The members of the establishment committee appointed pursuant to Article 3 of the Addenda to the Act may, with approval from the Administrator of Veterans Affairs, meet expenses necessary for the establishment of the Corporation out of the property that is to vest in the Corporation pursuant to Article 4(2) of the Addenda to the Act.

Article 4 (Value of State Property Vested in the Corporation)
The value of State property and goods vested in the Corporation pursuant to Article 4(1) of the Addenda to the Act shall be their book value at the time of vesting.

Article 5 (Applications for Succession to Rights and Obligations of the Association for Support of Veterans Organizations and Others)
Applications for succession to the rights and obligations of the Association for Support of Veterans Organizations and the Veterans Scholarship Association, an incorporated foundation, under Article 7(1) of the Addenda to the Act shall be made within three months from the date this Decree enters into force.

Article 6 (Establishment of a Partnership)
A person intending to establish a partnership under the Civil Act pursuant to Article 8(2) of the Addenda to the Act shall obtain permission from the Administrator of Veterans Affairs within six months from the date of establishment of the Corporation.

Article 7 (Relationship to Other Statutes and Regulations)
After the establishment of the Corporation, "National Veterans Hospital" and "Director of the National Veterans Hospital" in the Organization of the National Veterans Hospital, the Regulations on Medical Treatment for Disabled Military Personnel and Police Officers, and the Regulations on Special Medical Treatment at the National Veterans Hospital shall be construed as "Veterans Hospital" and "Director of the Veterans Hospital," respectively, and "State medical facilities" in Article 15 of the Military Veterans Assistance and Compensation Act and Article 15 of the Military Veterans Assistance and Compensation Benefits Act shall be deemed to include the Veterans Hospital.
